title: Security Hardening, Rate Limiting & Crowdsourced Incident Consensus Engine
goal: Eliminate critical vulnerabilities in the public anonymous access model: implement sliding-window rate limiting, strict Pydantic v2 bounding box validation, spatiotemporal clustering (DBSCAN/quorum), anti-griefing incident resolution tokens, and automated half-life decay workers.

issues.title: [Sprint 6] Strict Pydantic v2 Validation, Geographic Bounding Box Enforcement & Coordinate Sanitization
issues.description: Currently, `POST /api/v1/incidents` accepts raw dictionary payloads without Pydantic schema validation, allowing arbitrary coordinate injection and XSS payloads. Implement strict Pydantic v2 models (`IncidentCreateRequest`) with Metro Manila boundary validation (`METRO_MANILA_STRICT_BBOX` [120.90, 14.35, 121.15, 14.80]), sanitize free-text descriptions using Bleach or regex, and reject NaN/infinite/out-of-bounds coordinates with HTTP 422.
acceptance_criteria: `IncidentCreateRequest` schema strictly typed in `backend/app/schemas/telemetry.py`
Coordinates outside Philippine/Metro Manila bounds are rejected with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
XSS injection strings (`<script>`, `<iframe>`) in description fields are stripped and sanitized
Unit tests in `backend/tests/test_security.py` confirm rejection of malformed or out-of-bounds payloads

issues.title: [Sprint 6] Sliding-Window IP & Fingerprint Rate Limiting for Spatial Endpoints
issues.description: Geospatial queries (`ST_DWithin`, route snapping, incident queries) are computationally expensive. Implement an in-memory / Redis-backed sliding window rate limiter middleware in FastAPI to protect spatial endpoints from denial-of-service. Enforce limits: max 60 route analyses/minute per IP, max 5 incident reports/10 minutes per IP, returning standard HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with `Retry-After` headers.
acceptance_criteria: FastAPI middleware tracks request rates using client IP and optional forward proxy headers (`X-Forwarded-For`)
Exceeding rate threshold triggers HTTP 429 with JSON payload containing retry countdown
Whitelisted internal health check (`/api/v1/health`) bypasses rate limiting
Automated tests verify that burst requests beyond threshold are throttled

issues.title: [Sprint 6] Spatiotemporal Incident Clustering & Corroboration Engine (150m / 15m Quorum)
issues.description: Single anonymous reports should not immediately become high-severity confirmed alerts. Implement a spatiotemporal clustering service (`IncidentConsensusEngine` in `backend/app/services/incident_consensus.py`) that clusters reports within a 150-meter spatial radius and 15-minute window. Single reports are assigned `status: REPORTED` (confidence 0.35); corroborating reports from distinct IPs escalate the cluster to `status: VERIFIED` (confidence 0.75+).
acceptance_criteria: New reports within 150m and 15 minutes of an active incident increment corroboration count rather than creating duplicate markers
Corroboration increases confidence score from initial 0.35 up to 0.98
Status promotes from `REPORTED` to `VERIFIED` upon receiving 2+ independent reports or verified agency source (MMDA)
Frontend renders unverified reports with dashed outline and `[UNVERIFIED]` badge

issues.title: [Sprint 6] Tamper-Resistant Incident Lifecycle & Protected Resolution (Reporter Token & Community Vote)
issues.description: Currently, anyone can call `PATCH /incidents/{id}/resolve` and clear real active road hazards. Introduce anti-griefing controls: when an incident is created, return a cryptographic session token (`reporter_token`) stored in the reporter's localStorage, permitting the original author to mark it resolved within 15 minutes. For general commuters, implement a confirmation voting mechanism ('Is this road clear? [STILL THERE] / [CLEARED]'). Only a net clearance score of +3 moves status to `RESOLVED`.
acceptance_criteria: `POST /incidents` returns an ephemeral `reporter_token` enabling immediate author clearance
Unauthenticated third parties must submit clearance votes via `POST /incidents/{id}/vote-clearance`
Net clearance threshold (clear votes - active votes >= 3) triggers automatic transition to `CLEARING` and `RESOLVED`
Frontend displays 'Still Active' vs 'Cleared' confirmation buttons on incident cards

issues.title: [Sprint 6] Automated Incident Aging, Half-Life Confidence Decay & Garbage Collection Worker
issues.description: Prevent stale or abandoned incident reports from permanently clogging road corridors. Implement an asynchronous background worker task running every 60 seconds that applies exponential half-life decay to active incident confidence scores ($T_{\text{half}} = 20$ minutes for unverified, $60$ minutes for verified accidents). When confidence drops below 0.15 without fresh corroboration, transition incident to `status: EXPIRED` and remove from active route delay calculations.
acceptance_criteria: Background task periodically iterates over active incidents and recalculates time-decayed confidence
Uncorroborated single-reporter incidents auto-expire after 30 minutes of inactivity
Expired incidents are archived in database and excluded from `/api/v1/incidents` active queries
Route analysis automatically recalculates when an incident expires along a monitored corridor
